text.name: Buttons are interactive elements that allow users to take actions, such as submitting a form, navigating to a page, or performing a specific task.
Different button styles designed for different hierarchy levels and use cases.
Used for the main action or most important tasks.
Used for secondary actions or multi-button layouts.
Used for less prominent secondary options or utility links.
Used for minimal emphasis or standalone group items.
Used for inline text links or minor system navigations.
Used for inline text links or minor system navigations.
Each button variation supports native state changes for interactive completeness.
Buttons are available in multiple sizes to fit different layouts and use cases perfectly.

• This is the main Button Component Set and serves as the single source of truth. • All button variations (Primary, Secondary, Secondary Grey, Tertiary, Tertiary Grey, Link) use the same interaction states and sizes. • Any change to a state’s color, typography, spacing, or radius will automatically update all button sizes, icon variations, and instances. • Do not manually edit individual button instances. Update the main component, design token, or variable to ensure consistency.

• Maintain consistent color usage and interaction behavior across all variations. • Hover state is primarily for desktop interactions. • Focus state should provide a clear keyboard-accessible indication. • Use the component set and variants for all use cases to ensure consistency. • Make changes only in the main component set or related design tokens/variables.

Use Brand/Button/{type}/{property}/{state}. Variables are bound to all painted button fills, labels, loading indicators, borders, and focus rings. Empty/transparent properties remain unpainted.
Keep Brand/Base/* and Brand/Blue/* as primitive source names. Use color/text/*, color/background/*, and color/stroke/* as semantic aliases in product designs.
